downstream_details.affected_use: 1.2 **The actual surviving-head calculation.** Fix $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and let $M=f_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$, or $M=e_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$. The local residue theorem [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] says $M=0$ exactly when the corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise its head is the simple $L(C)$ at that edge, and it is self-dual. The ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ is closed under the two crystal operators by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], so $C$ is standard. The actual detector/corner Hom comparison of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] applies to maps from a Std-head object to a Std-socle object. Applying it to $M$ and $L(B)$ for each standard $B$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_H(\pi M,D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,L(B))$, of dimension $\delta_{CB}$. Since the $D(B)$ are the complete distinct Hecke simples, this computes the head of $\pi M$ as the single simple $D(C)$ and proves $\pi M\ne0$. The natural intertwining of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]] identifies $\pi M$ with the appropriate Hecke translate of $D(A)$, and its natural duality comparison makes that translate self-dual. Its socle is therefore also $D(C)$. A direct sum of two nonzero finite-length modules has at least two nonzero simple head summands, so a module with simple head is indecomposable. If the edge is absent the translate is zero by the same natural isomorphism. This proves (iii) in both directions by a Hom calculation; no arbitrary head or socle preservation by an exact quotient is assumed. [F2, given, construct, algebra]
